scenes.title: Four Aims in Character
scenes.summary: Characters must be good, appropriate, like, and consistent: Menelaus in the Orestes, Odysseus' lament in the Scylla, Melanippe's speech and Iphigenia at Aulis show the faults.

scenes.title: The Necessary and the Machine
scenes.summary: Character, like plot, must follow necessity or probability. The resolution must come from the plot, not from the machine as in the Medea and the departure in the Iliad; nothing irrational within the play.

scenes.title: Like Good Portrait Painters
scenes.summary: Poets should make their subjects better while keeping the likeness, as Homer did Achilles, and attend to what concerns the audience's perception.
